what: Realised per-token risk of C3a vs the raw 1 - alpha rule, one commit step per report-half teacher-forced decoder state (LLaDA-8B-Instruct, fp16)
stamp: exploratory; report half; teacher-forced decoder states
alpha_note: fixed before report-half numbers were read; the per-task C3a alphas of prereg/t12_grid_<task>.json were not committed, none added

eligible_sets.block32: masked rows of the leftmost non-empty 32-block of the region (primary)
eligible_sets.region: every masked row of the state

dense_alphas.grid: 160 log-spaced alpha in [0.005, 0.8] (rounded to 5 decimals, unique)
dense_alphas.note: traces the error-vs-tokens curves only; the reported grid is `alphas`

notes: Both rules commit a prefix of the same ell order, so the comparison at equal alpha is mostly a token-count effect: compare at equal tokens per state (arms[*][variant].matched_speed).
risk_unforced is taken over states where a position passed the bar; the unforced subsets differ between the rules, so it is not a like-for-like comparison.
Errors are against the reference token, not task accuracy.

notes.unforced: risk_unforced is the error of the commits in states where at least one position passed the bar; the unforced subsets differ between the two rules (the raw rule has fewer forced states at the same alpha), so unforced risks are not a like-for-like comparison.  unforced_over_alpha = risk_unforced / alpha: under 1 means the nominal bound holds on those commits.

matched_speed.note: dense alpha grid: traces the curves only; matched = risk interpolated at fixed tokens/state inside every bootstrap draw (draws whose tokens range misses T are dropped from the CI)
